audience: Frontend engineers onboarding to the micro-frontend composition model

mode_descriptions.build_time: Monorepo composition: host imports remotes as turborepo workspace packages at build time; one bundle, one deploy; remotes versioned by the lockfile
mode_descriptions.runtime: Zone composition: an edge/zone router stitches independently-deployed remotes at request time (zones / module federation); each team ships its own bundle

flows.name: Page Load (host pulls remotes)
flows.purpose: User hits a route → host shell renders → it composes the viewer + search remotes (imported at build time, fetched at runtime) → each remote calls the BFF for its own data.
step_outline: zone_router → host    : route to host shell (single app vs zone-mapped)
host → viewer         : mount @rask/viewer (import build_time · fetch runtime)
bff → browser         : hydrated shell + composed remotes painted

flows.name: Cross-App Event (events up / props down)
flows.purpose: A click in @rask/search must drive @rask/viewer. The remote emits an event up to the host's shared bus; the host pushes new props down to the sibling remote. No remote imports another.
step_outline: search → host   : emit event up · {type: 'result.selected', line_id}
host → host     : shared bus · update URL-as-state (?line=…)
host → viewer   : props down · {line_id} (re-render, no remount)
host → zone_router: push URL so a refresh/deep-link restores state

flows.name: Auth Handshake (Keycloak OIDC)
flows.purpose: The host owns the session; remotes never see Keycloak directly. Host attaches the token; the BFF validates it once per zone.
step_outline: host → bff      : OIDC redirect / token exchange (Keycloak)
bff → host      : session cookie · access token in memory
host → viewer   : props down · auth context (token never in the remote's URL)

flows.name: Independent Deploy (runtime zones)
flows.purpose: Ship @rask/search alone without rebuilding the host. The zone router points its path at the new remote bundle. Runtime-only — at build time the whole app is one bundle and can't deploy a remote alone.

lessons: The host, viewer, and search all carry the user role (mint) — they are all frontend surfaces. They are told apart by label (@rask/viewer vs @rask/search), not by inventing a 7th color, and the BFF + zone router are the orch (sky) nodes.

build_time vs runtime is the composition-seam toggle, the one mode that matters here: same nodes, but the host either imports remotes as turborepo workspace packages (one bundle) or loads independently-deployed remotes via the zone router (module federation).

Cross-app communication is modeled explicitly: events up to the host's shared bus, props down to siblings, URL-as-state for deep-linking. No remote ever imports another remote — that is the rule the cross_app_event flow teaches.
Independent Deploy is runtime-only (only_mode='runtime'): in build_time mode the whole app is a single bundle, so you cannot deploy one remote in isolation.
The host owns auth: Keycloak/OIDC lives behind the BFF and the host passes an auth context down as props — remotes never carry the token in their URL, so build_time and runtime share one auth flow.
